decision.name: No defensible trigger
decision.rationale: Retained native Standard/Human evidence does not establish a natural Quarry Worker unlock: P38 has no live row at p688 and no native Quarry purchase or assignment through p10000, but it does not retain a cycle-by-cycle Jobs catalog stream. P43 starts with the row already unlocked after a test-only Construction intervention, and the late-game owner publication history is absent. JobsCycleInput also lacks the cross-owner work-cycle and generation envelope needed to qualify a trigger at a synchronous coordinator boundary.

candidates.proposedCondition: A Quarry Worker row becomes newly unlocked in the prepared Jobs publication, compared only with the immediately preceding Jobs owner publication.

standardHuman.triggerScope: P38 reports no native Quarry purchase or assignment through p10000 and the captured p688 Jobs input has no Quarry Worker row. It does not retain a cycle-by-cycle Jobs catalog stream, so transition frequency is not measured.

qualificationBlockers: P38 captured no live Quarry Worker row at p688 and reports no native Quarry purchase or assignment through p10000, but it does not retain a cycle-by-cycle Jobs catalog stream from which to count unlock transitions.
P43 first observes Quarry Worker already unlocked at p720; the preceding availability change is outside the Jobs trace and follows a test-only Construction priority substitution.
P43's later job assignment changes are not new unlocks and cannot serve as entry-point triggers.
P45 retains food-stock points without Jobs, Construction, queue, or owner-generation identities; P46's bounded late-game profile retains no prepared Jobs catalog stream.
Production JobsCycleInput does not carry a work-cycle ID, root generation, progression generation, or control generations for the captured rows.

candidates.reason: P40 proves the previous completed Construction intent and current Construction ordering are distinct publications. P43's later target changes are treatment-linked and do not create a same-cycle Jobs request.

Demand is computed lazily once per demand epoch and invalidated at cycle start or relevant mutation. The sample mixes owner-derived demand and reservations, carries no common owner publication identity, and does not express a player-selected goal or allocation request.

candidates.source: Captured native Build and Research queues
candidates.reason: Queue entries are explicit player commitments and are read when reservation sampling runs, but the queue source emits no independent owner event or shared owner-generation envelope for the Jobs boundary.
The callback reports an already prepared and successfully executed ordinary Jobs decision. It is not an independent request to coordinate or spend.
